newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany catches chemical weapon smuggler in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Germany catches chemical weapon smuggler in Beirut.

text.p: A Lebanese-born businessman wanted on an international arrest warrant for smuggling chemical weapons-making equipment to Libya was captured in Beirut on Monday, German police said.

The German federal crime office (BKA) in Wiesbaden said Berge Balanian, wanted for exporting state-of-the-art equipment to mix poison gases to Libya, was caught by Lebanese and German police at an airport cafe in Beirut.
"After intensive and extensive investigation and searching, the federal crime office succeeded in finding Berge Balanian in Lebanon," the BKA said in a statement.
"Lebanese authorities working with a BKA commando detained Balanian just before 1800 (local time) at the airport cafe in Beirut," the crime office said.
A spokeswoman for the BKA in Wiesbaden said it could take several days for Balanian to be extradited to Germany.
He had evaded capture in August when police arrested two other businessmen on suspicion of smuggling hi-tech equipment to Libya.
Police said 3.2 million marks ($2.15 million) worth of equipment to mix poison gases was sent to Libya from Germany between 1990 and 1993 in defiance of German arms control laws.
Prosecutors believe the equipment was bought by the businessmen's firms, then sent to Tripoli between 1990 and 1993 via Belgian companies owned by Balanian.
The German intelligence service BND has admitted it interviewed Balanian in the poison-gas case four years ago without discovering the deals.

Bonn clamped down on arms exports after German firms in the 1980s equipped a plant at Rabta in Libya suspected of making chemical weapons and enabled Iraq to extend the range of its missiles in the 1991 Gulf War.
Earlier this year U.S. officials accused Libya of trying to build a new chemical weapons plant underground at Tarhuna, 65 km (40 miles) southeast of Tripoli.
